I farm only 3.0 mu, so I will keep the land in the wheat-maize rotation I already know well instead of changing crops. I have 30 years of experience, my household is small, and I have well irrigation, so I will aim for steady output and manageable field work rather than anything risky. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put in moderate but solid fertilizer, irrigate at the key stages, and keep the field clean with a couple of pesticide sprays if needed. After wheat harvest, I will move straight into summer maize on the same 3.0 mu, use hybrid seed for stronger yield, keep fertilizer a bit heavier on nitrogen, and rely on timely water and basic pest control. I will keep tillage practical and labor-saving: rotary tillage for wheat season preparation, then mostly no-tillage or very light disturbance for maize after wheat so I can sow quickly and hold moisture.
